subject: Zeta committed capacity: TPS projection, SLO fit & headroom
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@zetacorp.com>

Cc: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@zetacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Zeta commitment planning — capacity inputs attached

Ethan / team,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. We're moving from a pilot to a committed Dedicated deployment and need a concise sizing recommendation to take to procurement. Attached is our expected traffic profile for Q1 (hourly token counts, percentile spikes).

Can you send:
- a short tokens/sec => GPU SKU mapping for the primary model we discussed (open-llm-XXL) and one smaller variant for fallback,
- p95 latency projections at target SLOs (200ms, 500ms),
- recommended commit (tokens/day or monthly commit) with a clear headroom buffer for peaks and holiday windows, and
- a one-page runbook (warmup/cache guidance + throttles/fallbacks) we can include in the contract.

Procurement will need this by EOD Friday to start redlines.

Attachment: zeta-traffic-profile.csv (CSV, 42KB)

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Director of MLOps, Zeta Corp

Samir — thanks for the profile. Looping in Karthik (capacity lead) and Kimberly (solutions) so we can give a compact, deal-ready recommendation.

Quick plan:
- Karthik will produce a concise tokens/sec -> GPU mapping and p95 latency estimates for the model variants you listed.
- Kimberly will draft the one-page runbook (warmup, KV caching, fallback model map) and include guidance for autoscale/burst windows.
- We’ll include two commit options: a conservative commit (baseline + 25% headroom) and a peak-safe commit (baseline + 50% headroom) plus explicit holiday buffer.

Can you confirm whether the attached profile includes 24/7 steady traffic or if there are planned batch windows? That changes how much warmup/cold-start headroom we recommend.

We’ll target delivery by Thursday COB to give procurement Friday. If you’d prefer, we can also do a 30-minute walkthrough Thursday morning.

Cheers,
Ethan Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@zetacorp.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Zeta commitment planning — capacity inputs attached

Samir/Ethan — attaching the initial sizing note. Key bullets below; see attached PDF for the math and assumptions.

Attachment: zeta-inference-sizing-v1.pdf (PDF, 168KB)

Summary (model: open-llm-XXL; fallback: open-llm-LARGE):
- Baseline observed (from your CSV): median sustained ~12k tokens/min (~200 TPS) during business hours; 99th percentile short spikes to ~90k tokens/min (~1,500 TPS) for brief bursts.
- Throughput mapping (conservative kernels, quantized runtime):
  - open-llm-XXL @ float16 on A100 equivalent: ~450 tokens/sec per GPU at p95 in steady single-tenant mode (no aggressive batching).
  - quantized/open-kernel variant on T4-like profile: ~220 tokens/sec per GPU for fallback LARGE model.
- SLO fit estimates:
  - To meet p95 <= 500ms for majority of user requests, plan for ~3x steady-state GPU capacity vs median TPS to absorb variance and KV cache misses (this includes continuous batching headroom and warmup).
  - For p95 <= 200ms target, increase to ~4.5x median capacity; this is tighter and drives cost materially higher.
- Recommended commit options (monthly tokens):
  - Option A (Operational): commit sized for median * 3 headroom — estimates to cover sustained hours + typical spikes. (We list the concrete tokens/month in the attached PDF table.)
  - Option B (Peak-safe): median * 5 includes holiday + unexpected adoption surges; recommended if you need SLA-backed latency during marketing events.
- Holiday buffer: add explicit +10% during Dec–Jan windows (or mark as reserved burst capacity).
- Runbook highlights: warm cache by staging traffic during shift start, pre-warm common KV prefixes for top-100 prompts, fallback routing to LARGE model under sustained queueing, and token budget throttles for non-critical endpoints.

Sizing example quick math (illustrative):
- 1,500 TPS peak => to sustain with open-llm-XXL at 450 TPS/GPU requires ~3.4 GPUs; with 3x safety we'd provision 11 GPUs for short peaks.
- Continuous-batch improvements (prefix caching + 4-request batching) can reduce effective token cost by ~1.6x in typical chat workloads; we account for this in the Option A numbers.

Open questions that change recommendation:
- Do you require hard p95 <= 200ms SLA? If not, Option A gives better unit economics.
- Any regional constraints (must run in us-east1 only) or on-prem requirements?

We’ll convert the PDF math into a single-slide summary for procurement if that helps.

—Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Rao <samir@zetacorp.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@zetacorp.com, Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@zetacorp.com>

Subject: Re: Zeta commitment planning — capacity inputs attached

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail procurement wanted. A couple of follow-ups: 

1) Procurement asked for two formal commit options expressed as monthly token commitments and associated reserved GPU SKU counts (we'll include the option we can sign). Can you translate Option A/B into: tokens/month + reserved GPUs + expected p95 at those commit levels (we need a one-paragraph justification for each)?
2) We want to add a 10% reserved buffer specifically for the Dec/Jan holiday window (call it dedicated burst slot). Please bake that into the Peak-safe option as an explicit line item.
3) Procurement also requested a 1-page runbook PDF they can include in the SOW — would you send that as a single file?

If you can get those three items by Thursday morning PST we can loop legal and procurement and start the signature workflow. Happy to take a 20-minute call Thursday 9:30am to walk procurement through the numbers.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of MLOps, Zeta Corp
